purpose: Development benchmark for tonality: Vinh's Tonality lesson (natural teaching as clean controls, his three bad-tonality demonstrations) plus the speaker's own flat and expressive readings of one paragraph. Provisional annotations; not independently listener-validated.
segmentation: Cuts fall in measured silences between words. Takes keep their internal pauses and the audio is not normalized. Cut points were chosen from Deepgram nova-3 word times and pauses measured from the audio; review them by listening.

marks.note: "Good morning, everyone" said with a sad face: subdued and flat, the wrong emotion for a greeting.

tonality.notes: A single 1.5 s phrase. Tonality is judged over 10-30 s passages, because one short line is too little speech to judge a voice by.

takes.note: Includes his acted disgust ("oh") while setting up the next exercise; that is expressive, not flat.

marks.note: "Good morning, everyone" said with a disgusted face: the wrong emotion for a greeting.

tonality.notes: A single 1.7 s phrase, too short to assess. It is also a wrong emotion rather than a flat voice; the detector does not judge which emotion a voice carries, because the emotion labels proved unreliable on natural speech.

marks.note: "Blank face Vinh": a deliberately emotionless delivery, the course's main tonality problem.

tonality.notes: The blank face is mostly visible, not audible. Its voice stays inside his normal teaching range on every measure tried: 11.2 semitones of pitch movement (teaching 10.7-14.8), the same loudness range and voice quality, audEERING arousal of 0.69 (teaching 0.51-0.79), and emotion2vec+ hears emotion in it as it does in his teaching. An audio language model rated it flat only while it could understand the words ("I don't have much emotion"); with the words filtered out it rated it like his teaching. Re-score it if a detector learns to hear it.

excluded.reason: A student's romantic passage, then a second take with Vinh calling out emotions over it, then applause. Another speaker, and the prompted emotions do not have to fit the words.

takes.note: Speaker-confirmed contrast with tonality-02: two readings of the same paragraph, this one the flat one.

marks.note: The whole reading stays on nearly one note; tonality-02 brings out the contrast between what employees know and the claim that few have delusions.
